narrative:
The model determined that you have a 31% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your requested loan duration, and the installment rate as a percentage of your disposable income. Your checking account status was the single most important reason for the denial. Having a negative balance (<0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show this status), and it pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk.

The other two top factors actually worked in your favor. Your shorter loan duration of 12 months is well below the 19-month average of approved loans, which helped reduce the risk score. Similarly, your installment rate of 2% of disposable income is lower than the 3% average seen among approved applicants, giving another moderate push toward approval.

Unfortunately, the negative signal from your checking account outweighed these positive aspects. 

To improve your chances next time, focus on clearing your checking account balance and maintaining a positive status for several months before reapplying. This single change would likely have the largest impact on future decisions. (198 words)
